$comment: Three ways to group the same 28 publications for the Atlas landing.
The landing used to open on all 28 frameworks at once, arranged by the
dependency spine. That put SP 800-53 at the top of everything, which is
not true: the top row of that picture was five unlike documents — a
control catalog, a threat knowledge base, an outcome framework, a federal
policy and a process — and the only thing they shared was that nothing
else in this corpus builds on them. That is a fact about our crosswalk
coverage, not a statement about the field, and drawn as a top layer it
read as a ranking.
So the landing groups first and drills second. Each lens answers a
different question about the same corpus, and none of them claims one
framework outranks another. The dependency spine still runs the level
below, where it is honest: 800-53 is the root of its own branch.
'kind' is a collapse of the publicationKind already recorded for every
catalog in src/ui/lib/catalogProfiles.ts, so membership is traceable to
an existing field rather than re-asserted here. tests/graph asserts every
publicationKind value maps to a family, so adding a new kind fails loudly
instead of silently dropping a catalog off the landing.
'job' is authored. No field in the corpus records what someone is trying
to do, so these placements are a claim about practice and should be read
as one. Each carries its reasoning.

families.label: Control catalogs
families.blurb: The requirements themselves, and the baselines that select from them

families.label: Risk and outcome frameworks
families.blurb: How to run the process and what good looks like when you do

families.label: Implementation and configuration
families.blurb: What to actually set, build, and check on a real system

families.label: Threat and defense knowledge
families.blurb: What attackers do, and what stops it

families.label: Programs and policy
families.blurb: The rules you are held to, and the programs that certify you meet them

job.label: By job
job.blurb: What you are trying to get done
job.$comment: Authored, not derived. See the file header.

families.label: Pick the controls
families.blurb: Decide what protections a system has to have
families.rationale: Everything that either states a requirement or tells you which requirements apply to your system.

families.label: Assess and authorize
families.blurb: Prove the protections are there and get a decision
families.rationale: The procedures you are assessed against and the programs that issue the authorization or certification at the end.

families.label: Harden a technology
families.blurb: Configure a specific product or platform correctly
families.rationale: Guidance written against actual technologies rather than against a control number, plus the identifiers that tie those settings back to controls.

families.label: Understand the threat
families.blurb: Know what adversaries do before deciding what to build
families.rationale: Catalogs of observed adversary behaviour and the defensive techniques mapped against it.

families.label: Design the architecture
families.blurb: Decide how the system should be shaped
families.rationale: Zero trust is an architecture decision made before control selection, not a control set — these three are read while designing, not while assessing.

families.label: Govern the program
families.blurb: Set direction and report on it across a whole organization
families.rationale: Written for the people accountable for a programme rather than for a single system: outcomes to steer by, and the governance frameworks for AI.
